SHRI.JITHIN LUKOSE  SRI.M.S.MOHAMMED ANSARY  SRI.P.SAMSUDIN  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 10.07.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO. 2421 OF 2016  3  2025:KER:50755  JUDGMENT
This appeal is filed by the insurance company/3 rd respondent in O.P (MV) No.584 of 2012 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Manjeri.
The respondents herein are the petitioners/claimants before the tribunal.

2. According to the respondents/claimants, on 14.01.2008 at about 09.45 pm, while the deceased was walking through the public road, a maruti car bearing registration No.KL-10-U-8816 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit against the deceased.
As a result of the accident he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on 22.01.2008.
The appellants approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 4,57,000/-, limited to 4,00,000/-.
3. Before the tribunal, the 1st respondent is the driver, 2 nd respondent is the owner and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Respondents 1 and 2 remained ex parte before the National Insurance Company Limited vs Macheri Jameela on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62965088/
2 tribunal.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs Macheri Jameela
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The 3rd respondent insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy, but both the quantum of compensation claimed and the allegation of negligence.
Before the tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced on either side.
Exts.A1 to A8 were MACA NO. 2421 OF 2016 2025:KER:50755 marked.

The tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 15,93,600/- rounded to 15,94,000/- as compensation under different heads with interest @9%
per annum from the date of petition till realization with proportionate costs from the 3rd respondent-insurer.
Challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the 3rd respondent, insurer has come up in appeal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the respondents/claimants and the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/insurer.
5.

The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company mainly challenged the following heads :-
Notional income :- On a perusal of the award, it is seen that the tribunal has fixed the income of the deceased as 4,000/-.

The learned counsel appearing for the claimant submitted that going by the judgment in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the notional monthly income of the deceased ought to have been fixed at 6,500/- whereas the learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the income arrived at by the tribunal is just and reasonable.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Ltd. [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that no cross objection has been filed by the claimants.

Since the Motor Vehicles Act is a MACA NO. 2421 OF 2016 2025:KER:50755 welfare legislation, following the judgment in Ramachandrappa (supra), in order to award just compensation, I find it is appropriate to refix the monthly income as 6,500/-.
Compensation for loss of dependency :-

The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the tribunal has added 50% towards future prospects to the income fixed,
instead of 25% since the deceased was 40 years at the time of death.

The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company relied upon the claim petition as well as the postmortem certificate issued by the hospital, wherein the age of the deceased was shown as 40 years and submitted that the the future prospects to be added is 25% and not 40% since the deceased was not below 40 years.
In the postmortem certificate also the age is shown as 40 years.
Since, there is no other document to prove the age of the deceased, I find that the age mentioned in the postmortem report is to be taken.
Accordingly, the age of the deceased is fixed as 40 years.

Going by the judgment in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC)] and Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC), the claimants are entitled to get only 25% of the income fixed towards future prospects, since the age of the MACA NO. 2421 OF 2016 2025:KER:50755 deceased comes with the age group between 40 - 45 years and not below 40 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors [2017 (4) KLT 662 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [2010(2) KLT 802(SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Standing Counsel for the insurance company further submitted that, although there were six legal heirs, the tribunal erroneously deducted 1/6th towards personal expenses, instead of 1/4th.

The learned standing counsel for the insurance company submitted that going by the judgment in Sarla Verma (supra), when the number of legal heirs exceeds six, the deduction towards National Insurance Company Limited vs Macheri Jameela on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62965088/
3 personal expenses is 1/5th.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs Macheri Jameela
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since in the present case, there were only six legal heirs, I find that the appropriate deduction to be made towards personal expenses is 1/4th.

Since the notional income is fixed at 6,500/-, by adding 25% towards future prospects, the income is recalculated as 8,125/-
for the purpose of awarding compensation under the head loss of dependency.
Therefore, the compensation payable under the said head is recalculated thus: 10,96,875/- (8,125x12x15x3/4).
The tribunal has already paid an amount of 9,00,000/- under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 1,96,875/- under the head loss of dependency.
Compensation for funeral expenses :-

The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that going by the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants are MACA NO. 2421 OF 2016 2025:KER:50755 entitled only for a total compensation 15,000/-.
The tribunal has awarded an amount of 25,000/-.
Therefore, there will be a deduction of 10,000/- under the afore head.
Compensation for loss of estate :-
The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that going by the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants are entitled only for a total compensation 15,000/-.
The tribunal has awarded an amount of 1,00,000/-.
Therefore, there will be a deduction of 85,000/- under the afore head.
Compensation for loss of consortium/ loss of love and affection :-.
The learned standing counsel for the claimants submitted that the tribunal has awarded only an amount of 1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium.
Considering the fact that there are six legal heirs, going by the judgment in Pranay Sethi (supra), I find that the claimants are entitled for a total amount of 2,40,000/- (40,000x6).
Therefore, there will be an additional amount of 1,40,000/- under the head loss of consortium.

The learned standing counsel appearing for the insurance company submitted that the tribunal has awarded an amount of 4,50,000/- towards loss of love and affection, which is against the MACA NO. 2421 OF 2016 2025:KER:50755 principle laid down in the judgment in New India Assurance Company v. Somwati and others [2020 (5) KLT OnLine 1198 (SC)], wherein it has been held that once compensation is awarded under the head loss of consortium, no amount shall be awarded under the head loss of love and affection, as it would to duplication of compensation.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company v. Somwati and others [2020 (5) KLT OnLine 1198 (SC)]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence I am inclined to delete 4,50,000/- awarded under the said head.

6. Though the appellants challenged the compensation under other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.

7. Thus, the impugned award of the tribunal is modified as follows:

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and the claimants are awarded a total compensation of 13,85,475/- (Rupees Thirteen lakhs eighty five thousand four hundred and seventy five only) with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs.
The appellant-insurer shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The claimants shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the respondent insurer within a period of one month so as to enable the insurance company to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to MACA NO. 2421 OF 2016 2025:KER:50755 furnish details as above, it shall be open for the insurance company to deposit the said amount before the tribunal.

Upon such deposit being made, the National Insurance Company Limited vs Macheri Jameela on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62965088/
